catalog_quote: Nandris 1959 section 4 (pp. 9-10): "The OCS texts, with the exception of the Kiev Miss., do not mark the quantity or the stress. The Kiev Miss, frequently uses diacritic signs over vowels ... these signs were probably intended to indicate the quantity or the stress, though they are used inconsistently. ... There is, however, no direct evidence concerning quantity, stress, and intonation in the historical period of OCS. It is, moreover, only by a comparative study of stress and intonation (or quantity) in the modern Slavonic languages, especially in Russian and Serbo-Croat, that one can conclude that CS had a free (movable) expiratory stress and a musical intonation (pitch). This could be either acute (rising ') or circumflex (rising-falling ~). ... In CS, these three phonemic elements (quantity, stress, intonation) were independent of each other, i.e. an unstressed vowel could be long, …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Nandris 1959 sec. 4 quotation is verbatim in the held archive.org text layer at the stated section and running head (pp. 9-10); the De Bray supporting quote is verbatim too (page is 3, not 4 -- cosmetic). (2) Deciding source is a 1959 reference grammar (Glottolog 'grammar', 235 pp) with a dedicated stress section; for a dead manuscript language the only possible finding is 'stress not recorded in the texts; Common Slavic free mobile stress with pitch reconstructed comparatively', and every other grammar opened now says the same: Vondrak 1912 p. 75 ('Über den Akzent im Aksl. wissen wir nichts Sicheres, da er... nicht bezeichnet wurde'), Leskien 1919 sec. 5 (quantity 'nicht überliefert'), Schenker 1995 sec. 3.18 and n. 333 (held), and the newest open-access grammar, Polivanova 2023 p. 411 n. 25 (accentual properties 'remain unobservable or unknown for OCS').

sources.citation: Leskien, August. 1919. Grammatik der altbulgarischen (altkirchenslavischen) Sprache. 2.-3. Aufl. Heidelberg: Winter. (archive.org grammatikderaltb00leskuoft)
sources.quote: 'Die Silbenquantität ist nicht überliefert. Welche Vokale ursprünglich lang, welche kurz waren, lehrt die vergleichende Grammatik der idg. Sprachen.' No section on word accent placement in OCS proper; accent discussed only as Ursl./Balto-Slavic intonation in historical phonology.
sources.locator: sec. 5, pp. 4-5; also p. (line 12651) 'Da die Quantität des Ab. nicht überliefert ist'

sources.citation: Polivanova, Anna. 2023. Old Church Slavic: Grammar and Dictionaries. Transl. Lev Blumenfeld, ed. Artemij Keidan. (Biblioteca di Studi Slavistici.) Firenze: Firenze University Press. Open access (OAPEN 20.500.12657/74795).
sources.quote: 'Recall that many characteristics of suffixes that could be taken as evidence for or against unification remain unobservable or unknown for OCS; primarily, these are the accentual properties.' Clitics: 'From comparative Slavic grammar we know that clitics have particular accentual properties.' No OCS stress rule is given anywhere (grep of stress/accent/prosod over the whole book).
sources.locator: p. 411 fn. 25 (ch. 23 'Formative inventories'); also clitics section (text line 35036)

sources.citation: Vondrák, Václav. 1912. Altkirchenslavische Grammatik. 2. Aufl. Berlin: Weidmann. (archive.org text layer)
sources.quote: 'Akzent. Über den Akzent im Aksl. wissen wir nichts Sicheres, da er in den aksl. Denkmälern nicht bezeichnet wurde. Die Kiever Bl. bilden in dieser Hinsicht eine Ausnahme. Man findet darin ein Akzent- und Quantitätssystem, doch ist es wohl kaum der Akzent und die Quantität nur eines bestimmten Dialektes ...' followed by a survey of the Kiev Folia marks (acute = accent word-internally, other signs = length) and 'in den aksl. Hauptdenkmälern finden wir nichts derartiges'.
